physical.notes: Printed switch-matrix drive column 3, return row 1. Switch Locations description "Trough Stack". The matrix page shades the cell 'Opto, Typically Closed'. It is position JAM BALL of the Trough IR LED board A-18617-1 and the Trough IR Photo Transistor board A-18618-1 (LED1 on J1-7, photo transistor Q1 on J1-3), wired to the 16-Opto Switch Board A-16998.1 at J1-9 and J2-10. Projection: the table models no trough-stack (jam) position; the manual's trough boards put the jam-ball opto at the eject end of the outhole trough, so it is projected onto the eject-end trough kicker sw32. Retained script: ReleaseBall (solenoid 14) pulses it each time it kicks a ball out of the trough.

Its public level is not a measurement of the contact; normally_closed records the grounded switch's open rest state.

Printed Fliptronic grounded switch F2 (Blue-Violet, J905-1 on the Fliptronic II board). An opto of the right Flipper Opto Board A-17316 at the right cabinet button; the Fliptronic II pin list prints 'Blue-Violet, F2 to right flipper opto J1-2'. Each button's board carries two optos (F2 and F6), so one press interrupts both. WPC-Security reads the flipper column complemented (WPC_FLIPPERS returns ~swMatrix), so public 1 is the pressed button and the contact the column sees is open at rest: normally_closed is false. The matrix shades the cell as an opto. In the T.1 sweep a host write of 1 showed 'R. FLIPPER E.O.S.' (F1 BLK-GRN ORN) and fired the lower right flipper (public 45 and 46). The Flipper Opto Board's own pin list wires its J1-1 (Black-Yellow) from J905-1 and J1-2 (Blue-Violet) from J905-3, the J905 pins crossed against the Fliptronic II list; the wire colours and the opto positions agree, so the pin is a wiring detail. mechanisms.behavior: Three magnets on the Back Panel Assembly A-20033, the left (6, 20-10197), centre (5, 20-10197-1) and right (3, 20-10197-2) Coil Magnet/Breaker assemblies, each on an Opto Mounting Bracket A-20034 with an opto ahead of it: left (46), centre (47) and right (48). They throw the ball along the accelerator up the jump ramp (IPDB calls the toy a magnetic ball accelerator; the rules' skill shot and JUMP shots are shots up this ramp). The ROM fires each magnet once when its own opto is blocked: in T.16 BALL ACCELERATOR TEST a 150 ms pulse of 46 fired 6, of 47 fired 5 and of 48 fired 3, and a magnet that Enter had disabled fired nothing for its opto. Each magnet carries a thermal breaker that cuts it off when it overheats, and its opto must work for the magnet to capture and throw the ball (manual T.16). The retained known-working table approximates the throw: while a magnet's output is on, a ball over its trigger (LeftMagnet, CenterMagnet, RightMagnet) moving right is set to a fixed speed, and the ball is stopped past the right trigger when the centre magnet is on and the right one off; the ROM decides when each fires.
mechanisms.label: Magnetic ball accelerator

mechanisms.behavior: The Underside Ball Trough Assy. A-19948 carries a ball from the top of the playfield, behind the drop target and under the skull, to the lower right popper (manual T.18). It has two entrances, the left one behind the drop target (38, LEFT ENTR.) and the centre one (37, CTR. ENTR.); a ball passes POPPER 2 (42) and settles on POPPER 1 (41) in the Ball Popper Assembly A-19965, and the RIGHT POPPER coil (1) kicks it back onto the playfield. In T.18 UNDERGROUND TROUGH TEST the MANUAL mode pulses the DROP TARGET DOWN coil (8) as it starts and when 38 closes, so a ball can reach the left entrance; the AUTOMATIC cycle ejected a ball from the trough (14), fired the auto plunger (2) with the shooter lane switch (15) closed, and fired the popper (1) once 41 was held after 38, 37 and 42 had been pulsed. The retained known-working table holds the ball on the trigger sw41 and kicks it upward from there.
